answer: A meteg appears to be printed. It is most likely on the נ, beside its qamats, in this occurrence of כנפיך. Both the meteg and its host are uncertain. Without the meteg question, the pointing reads as כְּנָפֶיךָ.
visible_evidence: The whole word and the points below it are visible. Under the right-hand כ (which has a dagesh) there is a two-dot sheva. To the left of that is a T-shaped qamats, and just left of the qamats is a separate short vertical stroke. That stroke is not joined to the qamats stem, and it sits before the segol dots under the פ (which has a dagesh). The final ך has a qamats inside it. The stroke stands apart from the qamats crossbar, so it is probably a meteg rather than part of a vowel. However, at this enlargement I can't be certain whether it sits under the נ or at the right edge of the פ. I also can't fully rule out that it is a smudged point. No ink from the line below reaches it.
